newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - U.S. debt futures seen well supported.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - U.S. debt futures seen well supported.

text.p: Pullbacks in U.S. debt futures after last week's strong gains will probably be limited, given the market's relatively positive behavior near the highs, technical analysts said.

"Essentially, what we're building here in both markets (Treasury bonds and eurodollars) is more of a bull flag formation, only marginally retracing the strong advances from last week," said Eric Wall, an analyst at MMS International.
"The fact that we're hesitating near these recent highs is completely understandable...because we got a little over-extended," he added.
June T-bond futures were down about half a point on the day near 109-20/32 in mid-morning trade. They touched a high of 110-10/32 last Friday.

Although short-term momentum indicators have crossed into overbought territory, it was too early to say the up move was exhausted, Wall said, adding that weekly indicators were moving higher and should help buoy prices on pullbacks.
A logical downside projection for June T-bonds' correction would be 109-1/32, the 38-percent retracement of the most recent up leg from the April 28 low to last Friday's high, he said.
"Obviously, we can test that area but we should see some pretty good sponsorship there," he said.
Jim Bohan, a senior futures strategist at Merrill Lynch Capital Markets, said 108-1/2 or 109-00 should hold for now.
"It could stop here, it could possibly go another one-half to a point lower, but it's a countertrend reaction at this point," he said.

Wall at MMS said once the downward pressure stemming from the Treasury's note auctions this week moved out of the way, the contract should test the trendline drawn from early December highs, which today came in at about 111-17/32.
He also noted that that trendline would more or less coincide with the 50-percent retracement of the decline from the December highs to March lows.
In Eurodollar futures, the September contract should find support at 93.815, the 50-percent retracement of the rise from April 28 lows, Wall said.
That would keep the market above the mid-April peaks of 93.785, making the recent base pattern more viable, he added.
He noted, however, that September Euros needed to rise decisively above various old highs and congestion areas around the 94.00-level to turn the long-term trend upward.
